column1: # Defects that cannot exist on managed PostgreSQL, because creating them needs
# a real superuser and no managed service hands one out. AWS is explicit that
# rds_superuser is NOSUPERUSER on both RDS and Aurora; the true superuser is an
# internal service role no customer can connect as.
# These are not failures and not fixture bugs. The fixture is correct and the
# environment cannot host them, so the verifier reports them as n/a and leaves
# them out of its totals rather than counting them wrong.

column2: ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL turns off the internal foreign-key triggers, which needs a real superuser. session_replication_role = replica suppresses firing for one session but never sets tgenabled, which is what the detection counts.
CREATE FUNCTION ... LEAKPROOF is a superuser-only attribute, so the database has no LEAKPROOF function to find.

The state a failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY leaves behind cannot be reached inside a transaction, so the fixture writes indisvalid directly in pg_index, and writing a system catalogue needs a real superuser. The index stays valid here, and the 30 duplicate agent accounts it was meant to let through are skipped with it.
